minutes.headline: Planning Board split 2-2 on the Sunny Hill Road stormwater permit; the board backed a special permit for water-supply treatment plants.
minutes.summary: The board held a split vote on the 255 Sunny Hill Road stormwater permit (the fifth member could not vote), deferred it to Sept 9, and later learned from the planner that counsel treats a 2-2 tie as effectively a denial. It approved a Lancaster Avenue sign special permit and voted to send the Water Supply Protection District bylaw to hearing with a special permit requirement for new treatment works in Zone 1. It also sent the accessory dwelling unit bylaw to public hearing and approved the written decision for 240 Summer Street.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether to comment now or during the later discussion; chair asked to hold comments until the water district discussion.
Location of his existing 6-inch drain and a spring on the property line, drainage basin, and a request for no work on his property without written permission.

public_comment.stated_role: 50 Hemlock Drive, representing Hickory Hills landowners
public_comment.topic: Proposed adding swimming to permitted uses and edits to 2G and 2H in the Water Supply Protection District bylaw.
If boating is allowed then swimming should be too; supports a special permit as compromise.
Leave boating in; swimming is already covered as outdoor recreation.
Asked whether the state rules are laws or regulations.
Supports a special permit as a safety valve, citing a water district meeting interaction.
Special permit cost can be limited by getting public input before spending on engineering.
Special permits would slow the district; PFAS costs are large.
Asked the chair to complete a straw poll of the board.
Housekeeping questions on which draft edits are being carried forward.
A resident said the town should move to shared, collaborative document tools instead of many copies of documents.

budget_items.what_was_said: A water commissioner said the district must spend hundreds of thousands before coming to the board, so a special permit is a financial risk.
Board asked who pays; answered that water users pay through the district, and the town is also a water customer.
A commissioner said PFAS contamination will be very expensive and the district cannot fund it alone.

decisions.decision: Written-decision reviews for 240 Summer Street moved to later in the meeting.
Board followed the planner's advice to fix the hearing draft wording that night and schedule a special meeting to hold the hearing on September 23.
Board confirmed the public hearing date for the water bylaw as September 23.
Planner will revise the draft the next day and send it to the main commenters and the water district.
Planner asked Allison and Wilner to email their reasons for opposing the Sunny Hill permit so a written decision can be drafted.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board split 2-2 on the stormwater permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road, with one member abstaining, so the motion to approve did not carry.
The board then deferred the Sunny Hill Road decision to its September 9 meeting.
The board voted to send the Water Supply Protection District bylaw draft to public hearing, with a special permit requirement for new water treatment works.
The hearing on the water bylaw was set for September 23, after discussion of swimming, boating and who pays for treatment.
The board approved a signage special permit at 3 Lancaster Avenue and the written decisions for 240 Summer Street, and sent the accessory dwelling unit bylaw to hearing.

why_it_matters: A special permit step for new water treatment plants adds a review the water district would pay to prepare for, and water users and the town, as a water customer, would share those costs.
The accessory dwelling unit bylaw is headed to a public hearing and then to a town meeting vote, where residents may be asked to vote on it.
A tied vote on a stormwater permit leaves the applicant and the neighbors without an answer until the board decides again.

September 23 public hearing on the Water Supply Protection District bylaw and the accessory dwelling unit bylaw.

They differ on who submits the ADU draft, on who voted how on Sunny Hill, and on two hearing-closing votes that only our minutes record. Our minutes also carry cost figures the official minutes explicitly leave unprinted.
